summary: Live tenant 95p latency spike and intermittent 5xx after aggressive batching+quant profile; request safe rollback + snapshot hardening
description: Issue summary: BeaconAI reported a sudden increase in 95th and 99th percentile latency and a small but rising fraction of 5xx errors after enabling an aggressive combined config: async batching enabled (max_batch_size=256), prefix KV prefetch enabled, and a new quantization profile (int8-fast). Impact: customer-facing inference latency up ~2.2x 95p, request failures ~0.6% (5xx), sustained for ~20 minutes with intermittent recovery. Customer traffic is on a Dedicated pool. They requested prescriptive rollback steps that minimize user-visible disruption and guidance to harden snapshot restores to avoid recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On dedicated pool tenant BeaconAI, apply optimizer profile 'int8-fast-agg' which sets async_batching=true, max_batch_size=256, kv_prefetch=true, quant_profile=int8-fast
2) Route production traffic (baseline 1200 rps) to the tenant pool with normal token length distribution (avg 280 tokens).
3) Observe latency and error metrics over the next 5-30 minutes: 95p and 99p increase, occasional 5xx spike correlated with GPU memory pressure events and KV misses.

Request IDs sampled: rQf9-0a2b, rQf9-0a2c, rQf9-0a6d -> first byte delays 120-430ms; 5xx codes 502/504 observed
investigation_notes: Initial telemetry shows correlation between enabling async batching with very large max_batch_size and the quant_profile. Hypothesis A: int8-fast uses a kernel that increases GPU memory working set for long sequences and causes occasional OOM spills to CPU which amplify latency. Hypothesis B: aggressive batching caused large variance in sequence grouping leading to KV prefetch thrash and eviction storms. We validated via heap snapshots (linked PR) that memory footprint rose ~18% after profile change. No infra-level GPU hardware faults were reported. We flagged a candidate quick mitigation: reduce max_batch_size -> step down async batching -> revert quantization to conservative int8-balanced, while preserving some batching benefits.

2026-03-12T09:30 BeaconAI-Customer (support@beacon.ai): Thank you — we'll accept staged rollback with traffic split. Please confirm expected downtime (should be zero).
resolution: Workaround applied (in-progress): executed staged rollback with zero-downtime traffic-split to old optimizer profile. Sequence executed: 1) deploy profile gate: create 'BeaconAI-safe' profile copy with async_batching=true, max_batch_size=96, kv_prefetch=true, quant_profile=int8-balanced; 2) set routing policy: 80% live -> safe profile, 20% live -> previous aggressive profile for 10 minutes; 3) monitor 95p/5xx for 30 minutes; 4) if stable, shift to 100% safe profile; 5) capture final serving snapshot and tag snapshot with timestamp and profile metadata. We also hardened snapshot restores by adding a preflight check that verifies the quant kernel compatibility and available GPU memory headroom before completing restore (implementing a soft-fail to block restores that would trigger eviction storms). Outcome: after shift to safe profile, BeaconAI 95p returned to baseline within 18 minutes and 5xx rate dropped to baseline. Follow-up actions: a) propose an automatic pre-deploy memory smoke-test for aggressive quant profiles, b) add optimizer guardrail that caps max_batch_size by observed average sequence length per tenant, c) update canary checklist in Confluence page linked. Ticket will remain open until the guardrail PR is merged and canary metrics confirmed for 48h.
